result:
The diff only changes docs and a comment, so it can't cause a runtime bug. I found 4 low-severity documentation issues, under the 5-finding target because I didn't pad the list.

The core claim holds: `apps/web/app/services/` has no `urls.ts` at any level, and the templates import from `~/services/{{layer}}/{{name}}/urls`. Bash was denied after the initial diff, so the rest of the review used Read, Grep and Glob, and I ran no tests. None were needed for this diff.

```json
[{"file":"wiki/concepts/API Service Pattern.md","line":28,"summary":"The PR removed the 'self-contained' claim from the scaffold contract comment as overstated, but the canonical wiki page still says 'Each domain is self-contained: its own `urls.ts` and `index.ts`'.","failure_scenario":"A reader of the canonical service reference is told a domain is self-contained, yet generated `requests.ts` imports the layer's shared instance via `import {api} from '../api'` (.gaia/cli/src/scaffold/service.ts:731-732). That is the reason the third commit gave for dropping the claim. The same sentence now survives only in the page that shapes adopters' understanding, and it disagrees with the source comment this PR corrected."},{"file":"CHANGELOG.md","line":65,"summary":"The entry states flatly that 'the domain layer has none', but the 2.0.0 migration lets adopters keep `app/services/gaia/urls.ts` as their own file, so the claim is only true of the shipped template.","failure_scenario":"An adopter who upgraded through 2.0.0 and whose code uses the root file keeps it, per .gaia/migrations/2.0.0.md:506 and :692 ('a kept one is the user's own file'). Their layer does have a root `urls.ts`, so the entry is false for them. The wiki sentence and the contract note were the only places saying the scaffolder leaves that file alone, so they now have no statement that `/new-service` will not touch it. The behavior itself is unchanged: the scaffolder only writes `urls.ts` inside the service folder (.gaia/cli/src/scaffold/service.ts:785)."}]
```
